clue.text: City bank taken in by criminal owners

indicators.note: something taken in by another is swallowed up inside it, so one piece sits within the other
criminal suggests something crooked or bent, so the letters of the word it describes are twisted out of order

blocks.note: the letters of owners rearranged
to bank is to tilt or lean, as an aircraft does in a turn

explanation.surface: Crooked owners have pocketed a city bank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bank' tempts you towards a riverbank or a lender, but here it is the verb for tilting, as an aircraft does.
explanation.definitionFit: New Orleans is a major city in Louisiana, so it is an example of the general word.

clue.text: Sleep with American in Californian wine valley

blocks.note: a nap is a short sleep
A is a standard abbreviation for American, added on

explanation.surface: A tourist dozes with an American friend while touring wine country.
explanation.definitionFit: The Napa Valley north of San Francisco is California's best-known wine-producing region.

clue.text: Non-speaking part broadcast? Feel elated!

blocks.note: a walk-on is a small stage role with no lines
to air a programme is to broadcast it

explanation.surface: An actor thrilled that even a silent role is going out on television.
explanation.definitionFit: To walk on air is an idiom for being so happy you seem to float.

clue.text: Loony drinks French tea – with curled lemon?

blocks.note: a round is a set of drinks bought for a group
thé is the French word for tea
a twist is a curl of lemon peel used to garnish a drink

explanation.surface: Someone thinks French tea with a lemon curl is a mad choice of drink.
explanation.walkthrough: Round the twist is British slang for mad.
explanation.definitionFit: Round the twist is a British informal phrase for crazy, which loony also means.

clue.text: One Brontë admits exercising without effect

indicators.note: to admit is to let in, so one piece is let inside the other

blocks.note: Emily Brontë, author of Wuthering Heights
PT, physical training, is exercise

explanation.surface: One of the Brontë sisters confesses that her workouts are achieving nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: PT, physical training, is the old school name for exercise classes.
explanation.definitionFit: Done emptily means done in a hollow, futile way, with no real result.

clue.text: Granny piercing strong cotton cloth

blocks.note: nan is an informal word for grandmother
a keen wind is a piercing one

explanation.surface: Grandma pushing a needle through tough cotton fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Piercing' looks like it puts one piece inside another, but it is simply a synonym added after NAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Nankeen is a durable yellowish cotton fabric, originally made in Nanjing, China.

clue.text: Magazine's explosive content?

blocks.note: surface reading: a periodical publishing sensational stories
setter's reading: a magazine is also the cartridge holder of a gun, or an arms store, holding live rounds

explanation.walkthrough: Magazine suggests a glossy publication with explosive revelations; the other sense is the part of a gun, or a store, holding bullets and shells.
explanation.definitionFit: Ammo is informal for ammunition, the cartridges and shells kept in a firearm's magazine.

clue.text: Seconds needed to crack extra code

indicators.note: to crack something open is to break into it, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: more means additional
s is the abbreviation for seconds

explanation.surface: Code-breakers say they need only a few more seconds to crack it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crack' and 'code' make a code-breaking picture, but the cracking is done to a word for extra.
explanation.definitionFit: Morse is the telegraph code of dots and dashes devised by Samuel Morse.

clue.text: Frenzied exposure besetting beloved princess? Tragedy

indicators.note: something frenzied is wildly agitated, so the letters of the next word are thrown into disorder
to beset is to surround on all sides, so one piece encloses the other

blocks.note: the letters of exposure rearranged
Diana, Princess of Wales, was widely known as Di

explanation.surface: A media frenzy around a much-loved princess ends tragically.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface recalls the press attention that surrounded Princess Diana.
explanation.definitionFit: Oedipus Rex is the tragic play by Sophocles about the king who unknowingly kills his father.

clue.text: Dua Lipa holds back an Asian dish

indicators.note: the singer's name holds the letters within it, so they are found inside running across the words
back tells us to read the held letters from right to left

blocks.note: letters running from the end of Dua into Lipa

explanation.surface: The pop star Dua Lipa keeps a rice dish to herself.
explanation.definitionFit: Pilau is rice cooked in stock with spices, a dish from South and Central Asia.

clue.text: Imagined a Parisian coming in for one flat

indicators.note: coming in for something means taking its place, so one piece replaces another

blocks.note: to picture is to imagine
un is French for a
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A Parisian pictured coming in to buy a flat.
explanation.walkthrough: In PICTURED, the I is swapped for UN.
explanation.definitionFit: A punctured tyre has lost its air, which is what a flat tyre is.

clue.text: That six-grand Terry Gilliam film?

blocks.note: first meaning: in British slang a monkey is £500, so twelve of them make £6,000
second meaning: the 1995 time-travel thriller directed by Terry Gilliam

explanation.walkthrough: Monkey is British slang for five hundred pounds, so six thousand pounds is twelve of them.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is both the amount of money in slang and the actual title of Gilliam's 1995 film.

clue.text: Former model moved with it

indicators.note: letters that are moved are shifted into new positions

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written, added to the fodder

explanation.surface: An ex-model has moved with the times.
explanation.definitionFit: Old-time describes something from an earlier era, which is what former means here.

clue.text: Check out organ in residence at college

blocks.note: the eye is the organ of sight
a student in residence at university is said to be up

explanation.surface: Checking out the organ in the college chapel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' only joins the pieces: the organ followed by the word for being in residence at university, as Oxbridge students are said to be up.
explanation.definitionFit: To eye up someone is to look them over with interest, the same as checking them out.

clue.text: Published rates dived appallingly

indicators.note: something done appallingly is done badly, leaving these letters in a mess

blocks.note: the ten letters used as fodder

explanation.surface: Published figures show interest rates have plunged terribly.
explanation.definitionFit: To advertise something is to make it public, so advertised and published both mean made known.

clue.text: Sumptuously rich cake left each tooth black, ruined with decay

indicators.note: something ruined is wrecked, so all the letters before it are broken up and rebuilt

blocks.note: L is the abbreviation for left
taken as written
taken as written
B is the pencil-grade abbreviation for black
taken as written

explanation.surface: An over-rich cake has left every tooth blackened and rotten.
explanation.walkthrough: All five pieces, the two single letters included, are shuffled together.
explanation.definitionFit: Death by chocolate is the name given to an intensely rich, many-layered chocolate cake or dessert.

clue.text: New converts without sin?

blocks.note: having no is being without
vices are sins or wicked habits

explanation.surface: Fresh converts to a faith are imagined to be free of sin.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits a playful idea: newcomers to a faith have not yet had time to pick up bad habits.
explanation.definitionFit: Novices are newcomers, especially new entrants to a religious order still in their probation.

clue.text: See 15
Shopper consumed by MDMA and booze: mistake

indicators.note: what is consumed by something is swallowed into it, so one piece goes inside another

blocks.note: E is slang for ecstasy, the drug MDMA
rum is an alcoholic spirit
to shop someone is to inform on them, and an informer is a rat

explanation.surface: An informer who took ecstasy and drank made a mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: To shop someone is British slang for betraying them to the police.
explanation.definitionFit: An erratum is an error, especially one listed for correction in a printed book.

clue.text: Buddhist figure – bloke a boy follows around

indicators.note: follows means comes after, so the second group of words is placed behind the first
turned around means facing the other way, so these words are read backwards

blocks.note: a bloke is a man
taken as written
a lad is a boy

explanation.surface: A boy trails a man around a Buddhist statue.
explanation.definitionFit: A mandala is a symbolic circular design representing the universe in Buddhist and Hindu practice.

clue.text: Design firm beginning to make model

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter only

blocks.note: Co is the abbreviation for company
first letter of make
to model for a picture is to pose

explanation.surface: A design firm starts making a model.
explanation.definitionFit: To compose is to create or put together a work, which is what designing does.

clue.text: Revolution about working in spiralling wind

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the first piece goes round the next

blocks.note: a cycle is one complete revolution
a machine that is on is working

explanation.surface: A rotating machine is working in a whirling gale.
explanation.definitionFit: A cyclone is a storm of winds rotating around a low-pressure centre.

clue.text: Sailor is returning bones

indicators.note: returning means going back the way you came, so is is read backwards

blocks.note: tar is an old word for a sailor
taken as written

explanation.surface: A sailor is coming home, with the old bones aching.
explanation.definitionFit: Tarsi is the plural of tarsus, the group of small bones in the ankle.

clue.text: Huge ungulate lacking oxygen and energy in river

indicators.note: lacking means going without, so a letter is taken away

blocks.note: a rhinoceros is a huge hoofed mammal
O is the chemical symbol for oxygen, removed
E is the symbol for energy, added

explanation.surface: A rhino struggles in a river, short of air and strength.
explanation.definitionFit: The Rhine is a major European river flowing from Switzerland to the North Sea.

clue.text: Agree to accept blame? Nothing's impossible!

indicators.note: to accept something is to take it in, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: to nod is to signal agreement
to carry the can is to take the blame
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Someone refuses to take the blame, insisting nothing is impossible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carry the can' is a British idiom for taking the blame.
explanation.definitionFit: No can do is an informal way of saying something cannot be done, a refusal like 'impossible!'.

clue.text: Book large and heavy from my perspective

blocks.note: first meaning: a big, weighty volume
second meaning, split in two: in my opinion

explanation.walkthrough: The second meaning is a two-word phrase run together, as in 'to me it seems'.
explanation.definitionFit: A tome is a large heavy book, and 'to me' means in my view.

clue.text: Mao and Stalin ordered French port

indicators.note: ordered means put into a new arrangement, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the two dictators' names, without the and

explanation.surface: Two communist dictators command a French harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ordered' reads as dictators giving orders, but it signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Saint-Malo is a walled port town on the coast of Brittany in north-west France.

clue.text: Muse appearing in encounter at Olympia

indicators.note: appearing in means showing up inside the following words

blocks.note: letters running across the three words

explanation.surface: A goddess is seen in an encounter at ancient Olympia.
explanation.definitionFit: Erato is one of the nine Muses of Greek myth, presiding over love poetry.

clue.text: Mysterious river ending in swamp

indicators.note: the ending of a word is its last letter only

blocks.note: the Dee is a river in Wales, England and Scotland
last letter of swamp

explanation.surface: A river with a mysterious end disappearing into a swamp.
explanation.definitionFit: Deep can mean profound or hard to fathom, which is close to mysterious.

clue.text: Create fuss: work as set-builder?

blocks.note: first meaning: cause a public commotion
second meaning, taken literally: construct a stage setting

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the literal second reading: a set-builder constructs scenery for the stage.
explanation.definitionFit: To make a scene is an idiom for causing an embarrassing public fuss.
